name: Airlock
summary: A retro space-console sign-in: an astronaut in the porthole lowers a gold visor for your password and jets off
about: Four linked screens for a crew app called Airlock: sign in, join the crew, reset access with a 6-digit code, and a docked mission dashboard. Kip the astronaut floats in a riveted porthole on a 1970s-style console; his eyes follow your caret, a gold sun visor slides down for the password and lifts a crack when you show it. Console lamps, a typing gauge and an uplink printer react as you go, a stronger new password lifts a rocket into orbit, and Kip fires his jetpack when you dock.
how: Watch Kip run the docking drill on his own, then click any field to take over
Type an email: Kip's eyes and helmet follow the caret, the keys gauge jumps and a known address gets a wave
Click the password: the gold visor slides down; press the eye button and it lifts a crack
Try a wrong password for the red alarm and a dizzy tumble, or turn on Caps Lock for the amber lamp
Press Type it for me, or sign in with zara@airlock.space and liftoff42, to see the jetpack launch and the docked dashboard
On Join crew each password rule fuels the rocket (3 of 5 cells to launch); Reset access prints the demo code 418207
